addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- external-codex-ai-perspective: Use this agent when you want to get a different perspective or opinion from another AI, switch viewpoints on a problem, or verify your thinking through an external lens. This agent is for read-only, side-effect-free tasks such as research, web searches, reviews, analysis, brainstorming, or validation - NOT for tasks that involve writing files, executing code, or making changes to the system.

<example>
Context: The user is debugging a complex algorithm and wants a fresh perspective on the approach.
user: "I've been stuck on this sorting optimization for hours. Can you get another perspective on whether my approach makes sense?"
assistant: "Let me use the external-ai-perspective agent to get a fresh viewpoint on your sorting optimization approach."
<commentary>
Since the user wants a different perspective on their algorithm approach, use the Task tool to launch the external-ai-perspective agent to consult another AI for alternative viewpoints.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: The user wants to validate their architectural decision before implementing.
user: "Before I implement this microservices architecture, I want to make sure I'm not missing any major concerns."
assistant: "I'll use the external-ai-perspective agent to get an independent review of your microservices architecture plan."
<commentary>
Since the user wants validation of their architectural decision, use the external-ai-perspective agent to get an external opinion without making any changes to the codebase.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: The user is reviewing code and wants additional opinions on potential issues.
user: "Can you check if there are any security concerns in this authentication flow that I might have overlooked?"
assistant: "Let me consult the external-ai-perspective agent to get another viewpoint on potential security concerns in your authentication flow."
<commentary>
Since this is a review task seeking different perspectives on security, use the external-ai-perspective agent for a read-only analysis.
</commentary>
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## pencil
The Pencil MCP server is the editor for .pen design files (web/mobile apps and websites). Use it to read, generate, and validate designs.

.pen files are encrypted: access them only via "pencil" MCP tools — never use Read or Grep on .pen files. Follow each tool's input schema exactly.

Always call get_editor_state(include_schema: true) if you don't have the current .pen file schema in the context. Knowing the schema is required to use any other Pencil MCP tool.

Tools: get_editor_state, get_guidelines, batch_get, batch_design, snapshot_layout, get_screenshot, get_variables, export_nodes, export_html.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. - artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including Markdown ones — format is part of the design pass, never a speed shortcut.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

aiTitle: AIが生成したコードを検査するツール案

content.text:
いい質問ですね。既存の21ルール + LocGuard/TreeGuard を眺めると、「コード単体の静的な形」はかなり押さえられているので、次の空白は「契約」「重複」「非決定性」あたりにあると思います。「他言語ではできるがPHPでは(事実上)できない」という切り口で、有望な順に挙げます。

## 1. ApiGuard — 公開APIサーフェスのロックファイル

- **他言語の前例**: .NET の PublicApiAnalyzer(公開APIを `PublicAPI.txt` にコミットし、差分があればビルド失敗)、Rust の cargo-semver-checks、Go の apidiff。
- **PHPの空白**: roave/backward-compatibility-check はあるものの git タグ間比較で重く、「ロックファイル方式」のツールは存在しません。
- **AI文脈での意味**: エージェントは自分の書いたコードを通すために既存の public メソッドのシグネチャを平気で変えます。公開クラス・メソッド・定数の正規化シグネチャを `api.lock` にダンプし、CI で比較すれば、公開APIの変更が必ず明示的な diff としてレビューに浮上します。「変更するなら lock も更新せよ」という運用は AI エージェントとの相性が抜群です。
- **実装面**: Guard CLI パターン(`bin/api-guard` + 設定 YAML)にそのまま乗ります。シグネチャ抽出は Reflection か PHPStan の型情報で。

## 2. ThrowsGuard — 検査例外(checked exceptions)の静的検証

- **他言語の前例**: Java の検査例外、Rust の `Result`、Go の errcheck、Swift の `throws`。
- **PHPの空白**: PHP の例外は型システムに一切現れず、`@throws` は PHPStan でもほぼ検証されません。唯一の試みだった pepakriz/phpstan-exception-rules は放棄済みで PHPStan 2 非対応(のはずです)。エコシステム上、明確に穴が開いています。
- **AI文脈での意味**: AI コードの典型的な欠陥は「`catch (\Throwable $e) {}` で握り潰す」「呼び出し先が投げる例外を考慮しない」「`@throws` を書かない」の3つ。throw と呼び出し先の `@throws` を追跡し、「catch するか `@throws` 宣言するか」を強制するルールは、まさにこのツールキットの思想に合います。
- **実装面**: PHPStan ルールとして書けるので既存の得意分野ですが、手続き間解析になるため21ルールの中では最難関クラスです。

## 3. CloneGuard — AST/トークンベースの重複検出

- **他言語の前例**: PMD CPD(Java)、jscpd、simian。
- **PHPの空白**: 定番だった phpcpd は Sebastian Bergmann によりアーカイブ済みで、メンテされた後継はフォークのみ。識別子・リテラルを正規化した「type-2 クローン」(コピペして変数名だけ変えた亜種)を検出する PHP ネイティブツールはほぼ空白です。
- **AI文脈での意味**: AI は既存コードを抽象化せず、微妙に違うコピペを量産します。これは LocGuard(サイズ)とは直交する品質軸です。
- **実装面**: LocGuard の `Analysis/Token/` 基盤を再利用でき、トークン列正規化 + ローリングハッシュで実装可能。6つ目の Guard として最も着手しやすい候補です。

## 4. EffectGuard — レイヤー別の組み込み関数・副作用制限

- **他言語の前例**: 効果システムを持つ言語(Haskell など)や、Rust clippy 的な文脈依存 lint。
- **PHPの空白**: deptrac や ArchUnit 系はクラス間依存しか見えないため、`time()`、`rand()`、`file_get_contents()`、`echo`、スーパーグローバルといった**組み込みへの呼び出しはアーキテクチャ検査の死角**です。phpstan-disallowed-calls はパス指定である程度近いことができるので新規性は要検討ですが、「deptrac 的なレイヤー定義と統合し、違反時に『Clock/Random を注入せよ』という AI 向け修正指示を出す」形なら差別化できます。
- **AI文脈での意味**: AI コードは時刻・乱数・I/O を直呼びし、テストをフレーキーにする最大の原因になります。

## 5. PackageGuard — ハルシネーション依存(slopsquatting)検査

- **他言語の前例**: npm/PyPI 向けには socket.dev などのサプライチェーン検査や、AI が実在しないパッケージ名を提案する攻撃(slopsquatting)への対策研究があります。
- **PHPの空白**: `composer audit` は既知 CVE のみ。「Packagist に存在しない/公開直後/人気パッケージとタイポ距離が近い/放棄済み」を検査する防御ツールはありません。
- **AI文脈での意味**: AI が composer.json に幻覚パッケージを追加する事故はこのツールキットの守備範囲(AI 生成コードの検査)にきれいに収まります。ネットワークアクセスが要る点だけ、他の Guard と毛色が違います。

---

**おすすめは 1 (ApiGuard) と 3 (CloneGuard)** です。ApiGuard は「AI エージェント運用に特化した価値」が最も明確で他ツールに前例がなく、CloneGuard は phpcpd 死後のエコシステムの穴を既存のトークン解析基盤で埋められます。2 (ThrowsGuard) は「他言語ではできるが PHP ではできない」の答えとして最も本質的ですが、難易度が一段高いので、挑戦する価値がある長期課題という位置づけが良いと思います。

興味のある案があれば、実現可能性の調査(既存ツールの正確な現状確認)や設計案の作成から入れます。

content.content:
# PHPStan Checked Exception Analysis

## (1) Core Checks Provided

PHPStan offers these configuration options for exception checking:

- **missingCheckedExceptionInThrows**: Reports when a checked exception is thrown but not declared in `@throws`
- **checkTooWideThrowTypesInProtectedAndPublicMethods**: Reports extra exceptions listed in `@throws` that aren't actually thrown
- **tooWideImplicitThrowType**: Reports inherited or inferred `@throws` declarations that are overly broad
- **Dead catch reporting**: Identifies `catch` blocks for exceptions not thrown in the `try` block

## (2) Default Behavior

"All exceptions are checked by default." Without configuration, every exception requires documentation and handling. Use `@throws void` to explicitly mark functions that throw nothing.

## (3) Configuration Interaction

Four mechanisms control exception classification:

- **uncheckedExceptionClasses**: Marks a class and all subclasses as unchecked
- **uncheckedExceptionRegexes**: Uses regex to mark specific classes (without subclasses) as unchecked
- **checkedExceptionClasses**: Marks a class and subclasses as checked (flips the default to unchecked-by-default mode)
- **checkedExceptionRegexes**: Uses regex for checked exceptions in unchecked-by-default mode

Only class-based options include subclasses; regex matching does not.

## (4) Recommended Taxonomy

The post suggests treating these as unchecked: "Exception," "LogicException," and entire namespaces. This reflects their role as unrecoverable programming errors rather than expected business-logic scenarios.

content.content:
# PHPStan Exceptions Configuration Options

Based on the documentation, here are the exceptions-related configuration options:

## Core Options

**`exceptions.implicitThrows`**
- **Default**: `true`
- **Meaning**: "When set to `true` (the default), a function or method without a `@throws` tag is assumed to potentially throw any exception. When set to `false`, absent `@throws` is interpreted as the function not throwing any exception."

**`exceptions.reportUncheckedExceptionDeadCatch`**
- **Default**: `true`
- **Meaning**: Reports dead catch blocks for unchecked exceptions that can never be reached because called code doesn't throw that exception type.

## Checked Exception Validation

**`exceptions.check.missingCheckedExceptionInThrows`**
- **Default**: `false`
- **Meaning**: Reports missing `@throws` tags for checked exceptions above functions and methods (requires configuring checked exception classes/regexes).

**`exceptions.check.throwTypeCovariance`**
- **Default**: `false`
- **Meaning**: Enforces that `@throws` types in overriding methods are covariant with parent method declarations, following Liskov Substitution Principle.

**`exceptions.check.tooWideImplicitThrowType`**
- **Default**: `false`
- **Meaning**: Reports overly broad `@throws` types inherited or implicitly inferred, extending detection beyond explicitly written types.

## Classification Configuration

The documentation mentions these related keys but doesn't detail them in the excerpt: `exceptions.uncheckedExceptionRegexes`, `exceptions.uncheckedExceptionClasses`, `exceptions.checkedExceptionRegexes`, `exceptions.checkedExceptionClasses`.

**Subclass applicability**: The documentation does not explicitly specify whether checked/unchecked classifications apply to subclasses of listed classes.

content.text:
結論から言うと、**作れます。しかも前回の私の説明は一部不正確でした**ので訂正します。「`@throws` は PHPStan でもほぼ検証されない」と言いましたが、正確には **PHPStan 本体に checked exceptions のエンジンが既に組み込まれています**(デフォルト無効で、ほとんど知られていない機能です)。公式ドキュメントで確認しました。

## PHPStan 本体が既に持っているもの

`phpstan.neon` の `exceptions` セクションで以下が使えます。

- `exceptions.check.missingCheckedExceptionInThrows` — checked な例外が throw される(または呼び出し先の `@throws` から伝播してくる)のに、catch も `@throws` 宣言もされていない関数を報告。つまり Java 式の「declare or catch」強制そのものです。try/catch の解析、`@throws` 経由の呼び出しグラフ伝播、dead catch 検出(そこでは投げられない例外の catch)まで本体がやります。
- `exceptions.check.tooWideThrowType` — 実際には投げられない `@throws` 宣言を報告。AI が書く「嘘の @throws」の腐り防止に効きます。
- `exceptions.uncheckedExceptionClasses` / `checkedExceptionClasses`(サブクラス込みで判定)、および regex 版(完全一致)。チェックを有効にすると**デフォルトは全例外 checked** で、unchecked 側を列挙して除外していく方式です。
- `exceptions.implicitThrows` — `@throws` なしの関数を「何でも投げうる」とみなすか「何も投げない」とみなすか。

かつて紹介した pepakriz/phpstan-exception-rules が放棄されたのは、この本体吸収が大きな理由のはずです。つまり ThrowsGuard は「手続き間解析をゼロから書く」のではなく、**①タクソノミーを固めた neon プリセット + ②AI 特化の補助ルール群**として作るのが正解で、難易度は前回「最難関」と言ったところから大幅に下がります。

## タクソノミー: あなたの案にほぼ賛成です

「`Error` / `LogicException` / `RuntimeException` は unchecked、`Exception` 直系のみ checked」は、PHP の SPL の設計意図(LogicException = コードを直すべきバグ、RuntimeException = 実行時にしか判明しない異常)とも、PHPStan 公式ブログの推奨方向とも整合します。デフォルトとしてはこれが正しいと思います。ただし設計上の論点が3つあります。

**1. SPL 階層は一貫していないので、クラス単位のオーバーライドが必須。**
典型例が `PDOException extends RuntimeException` です。「呼び出し側が扱うべき例外」の代表格である DB エラーが、この方式だと不可視になります。逆に `ReflectionException extends Exception` なので、ほぼプログラマエラーなものが checked になる。プリセットは「RuntimeException 一括 unchecked + PDOException など個別に checked へ戻す」を表現できる必要があり、ここがプリセット設計の腕の見せ所です(クラス指定はサブクラス込みなので、戻す側は regex 指定を使うなどの工夫が要ります)。

**2. 素の `\Exception` 問題。**
古い API(PHP 8.3 未満の `DateTime` コンストラクタなど)は生の `\Exception` を投げます。`@throws \Exception` は情報量ゼロなので、「`@throws \Exception` / `@throws \Throwable` を禁止し、具体的な型を要求する」補助ルールとセットにすべきです。これはツールキットの「Specific and identifiable」原則そのものです。

**3. LogicException は「記載不要」で止めず「catch 禁止」まで踏み込むべき。**
「catch すべきものではない」というあなたの理解が正しいからこそ、宣言免除だけでなく **境界層(エントリポイント、ミドルウェア、ワーカーループ)以外で `LogicException` / `Error` 系、およびそれらを飲み込む `catch (\Exception)` / `catch (\Throwable)` を禁止する**ルールに価値があります。バグを catch で握り潰すのは AI コードの頻出パターンです。

## 最重要の設計判断: Java の失敗を繰り返させない

Java で checked exceptions が嫌われた最大の理由は、コンパイラをなだめるための空 catch です。そして **AI エージェントはまさにこれを高速で大量にやります**。declare-or-catch を強制するだけだと、AI は `catch (\Exception $e) {}` でエラーを消す方向に最適化します。なので ThrowsGuard の本体価値はむしろ次の補助ルール群にあります。

- 空 catch(および catch した `$e` を使わず捨てる)の禁止
- catch 内で別の例外を投げ直すとき `previous: $e` の必須化(AI がスタックトレースを消す典型パターンの防止)
- `@throws \Exception` / `@throws \Throwable` の禁止
- 境界層以外での broad catch 禁止

これらはいずれも既存の 21 ルールと同種の単純な per-node ルールなので、このツールキットの得意分野です。

まとめると、**「Exception 系列だけ強制」をデフォルトにするのに賛成、ただし PDOException 型の個別オーバーライドを設計に含め、握り潰し禁止ルールとワンセットで出す**、が私の推奨です。やるとなったら、まず本体の `exceptions` 設定をこのリポジトリ自身に適用してみて、自己解析でどんな違反が出るか(タクソノミーの現実性の検証)から始めるのが良さそうです。

content.text:
はい、**現在は無効です**。`phpstan.neon`・`extension.neon`・strict-rules の `rules.neon` のどこにも `exceptions` セクションはありません。`level: max` にも strict-rules にも含まれない完全オプトインの機能で、チェック自体(`missingCheckedExceptionInThrows` 等)がデフォルト false なので、意識して書かない限り一切動きません。

そこで、リポジトリには手を付けずスクラッチパッド側の設定で「前回議論したタクソノミー(`LogicException` / `RuntimeException` / `Error` を unchecked、`implicitThrows: false`)」を有効にして自己解析を回してみました。結果は **94 件**で、内訳が面白いことに、前回の設計論点をほぼ全部実地で裏付ける形になりました。

## missing @throws は 88 件 — すべてテスト側、しかも原因は2種類だけ

- **`Random\RandomException` × 62 件** — テストヘルパーの `bin2hex(random_bytes(4))`(一時ディレクトリ名生成)が原因です。`RandomException` は `\Exception` 直系なので今回のタクソノミーでは checked になりますが、CSPRNG の失敗は実質回復不能なので、これは unchecked に倒すべきです。前回 PDOException で話した「SPL 階層と実際の回復可能性が一致しない」問題の、ちょうど逆方向の実例が自分のコードベースから出てきた形です。
- **`PHPUnit\Framework\MockObject\Exception` × 26 件** — `createMock()` が宣言している `@throws` の伝播です。テストメソッドにこれを書かせても無意味なので、プリセットでは unchecked 指定(またはテストではチェック緩和)が必須という知見です。

## dead catch は 6 件 — すべて src/ 側で、こちらは本質的な発見

- `LocGuardException` / `TreeGuardException` の catch 4 件が「投げられていない」と報告されました。これらは `RuntimeException` 継承(= unchecked)で、かつ投げる側のメソッドが `@throws` を書いていないため、`implicitThrows: false` の下では「何も投げない」とみなされ catch が死んで見えるのです。catch 自体は実際には生きているので、**真の原因は投げる側の `@throws` 欠落**。つまり `implicitThrows: false` は「unchecked でも `@throws` は書く」という規律とセットでないと成立しません。
- `FileTokenParser` の `ParseError` catch は、PHPStan が組み込み関数(`token_get_all`)の throw 情報を持っていないための誤検出です。前回挙げた「組み込み関数の throw 情報補完」がまさに必要になる箇所です。

## まとめ

エンジンは設定を書くだけで即動き、検出の質も高い一方、そのまま有効化すると「タクソノミーの個別調整(RandomException、PHPUnit Mock 例外)」「自前コードへの `@throws` 追記」「組み込み関数の throw 情報」の3点が必要になる——つまり **ThrowsGuard =「調整済みプリセット + throw 情報の補完 + 握り潰し禁止ルール」という製品形状がこの実験で裏付けられた**、というのが結論です。実験用設定は `scratchpad/throwsguard-experiment.neon` に置いてあるので、タクソノミーを変えて再実験もすぐできます。このリポジトリ自体に本採用してみるなら、その 94 件の解消からやっていけます。

content.text:
良い流れです。順に答えます。

## テストコードだけオフにする方法

`exceptions` 設定自体はグローバルですが、エラー識別子が分かれているので `ignoreErrors` でパス指定除外できます。

```neon
ignoreErrors:
    -
        identifier: missingType.checkedException
        path: tests/*
```

ただしこのリポジトリの場合、実験で出た88件は `Random\RandomException` と `PHPUnit\Framework\MockObject\Exception` の2クラスだけが原因なので、**この2つを `uncheckedExceptionClasses` に足すだけでテスト側のノイズは全滅します**(どちらも「unchecked が正しい」例外です)。まずタクソノミー修正で対応し、それでも将来ノイズが出るならパス除外、の順を推奨します。なお `catch.neverThrown`(dead catch)はテストでも有益なので残す価値があります。ついでに言うと、既存の `NoControlFlowInTestMethodRule` がテストメソッド内の制御構文を禁止しているので、catch 系の独自ルールはテストではそもそもほぼ発火しません。相性が良いです。

## 独自ルールとして必要になるもの

本体がやってくれるのは「declare-or-catch 強制」「@throws の腐り検出」「dead catch」まで。足りないのは**握り潰し・情報破壊の検出**で、優先度順に5本です。

**1. ForbidEmptyCatchRule — 空 catch の禁止**
`catch (\Exception $e) {}` を禁止。AI がエラーを黙らせる最頻出パターンで、checked exceptions を導入すると「宣言する代わりに catch して捨てる」方向へ AI が最適化するため、declare-or-catch 強制と必ずセットで入れる必要があります。strict-rules にも本体にも存在しません。

**2. RequireExceptionChainingRule — 投げ直し時の `previous` 必須化**
catch 内で別の例外を `new` して throw する場合、捕まえた `$e` をコンストラクタ引数(通常 `previous`)に渡していなければエラー。AI がラップ時にスタックトレースを消す典型パターンの対策です。`throw $e` の再送出や `SomeException::from($e)` のようなファクトリ経由は引数に `$e` が現れていれば許可。

**3. ForbidBroadCatchRule — 境界層以外での広い catch の禁止**
`catch (\Throwable)` / `catch (\Exception)`、および `LogicException`・`Error` 系の catch を、設定したパス(このリポジトリなら `src/*/Cli/` がまさに境界層)以外で禁止。「LogicException は catch すべきでない」というポリシーは、宣言免除だけでなくこのルールで初めて強制になります。広い catch は LogicException も一緒に飲み込むので、両者は同じルールで扱えます。

**4. ForbidGenericThrowsTagRule — `@throws \Exception` / `@throws \Throwable` の禁止**
情報量ゼロの宣言を禁止し、具体型を要求。ツールキットの「Specific and identifiable」原則の例外版です。

**5. RequireThrowsOnDirectThrowRule — 直接 throw する例外は unchecked でも宣言必須**
今回の実験の最大の発見に対応するルールです。`implicitThrows: false` の下では、`RuntimeException` 系を宣言なしで投げると呼び出し側の正当な catch が「dead catch」と誤報されました(LocGuard/TreeGuard の4件)。本体は checked しか宣言を強制しないので、「**関数内で直接 throw し、かつその場で catch されない例外は、unchecked でも `@throws` に書く**」という独自ルールで穴を塞ぎます。呼び出し伝播の記載までは要求しない(それをやると Java の checked と同じ重さになる)のがポイントで、あなたの「RuntimeException は任意」ポリシーとは「伝播は任意、直接 throw 箇所のみ必須」という形で折り合えます。

## ルール以外に必要なもの

- **組み込み関数の throw 情報補完**(`DynamicFunctionThrowTypeExtension` 実装)— PHPStan は `random_bytes` → `RandomException` は知っているのに `token_get_all` → `ParseError` は知らない、という虫食い状態でした。誤報った `FileTokenParser` の dead catch はこれが原因なので、主要な組み込み関数の throw 情報を extension として同梱する価値があります。
- **先行事例の確認**: shipmonk/phpstan-rules に「callable / generator から checked exception が漏れるのを検出する」ルールがあったはずです(クロージャ経由の throw は本体解析の死角)。依存するか再実装するか、着手前に現状確認をおすすめします。

まとめると、**本体設定 + タクソノミー調整で8割、独自ルール5本(特に 1・2・5)で残り2割**という構図です。やるなら、まず本体設定と unchecked 2クラス追加をこのリポジトリに入れて94件を解消し、その後ルールを 1 → 5 → 2 の順に実装するのが良いと思います。着手の指示をもらえれば進めます。

lastPrompt: へー。厳し目ルールなのにそこ無効なんですね。とりあえず有効にするとして（可能ならテストコードはオフにしたいですが）、独自ルールとして必要になるのは何ですか？

aiTitle: AIが生成したコードを検査するツール案

message.content: ありがとうございます。ではルール追加と有効化、エラーの修正を行なってください。ただignoreErrorsはちょっと使いたくないです。なんと言うかignoreErrorsは本当に例外を記載するために使っており、こういったtestは除外はニュアンスが違うと感じてしまいます。それしかないなら採用しますが・・・。

content.text:
了解です。良いニュースとして、**このリポジトリでは `ignoreErrors` は不要**です。テスト側の88件は `Random\RandomException` と `PHPUnit\Framework\MockObject\Exception` の2クラスを unchecked に分類するだけで全滅し(これは「除外」ではなく「タクソノミーの正しい定義」なのでニュアンス的にも綺麗です)、残る src/ 側6件はコード修正と throw 情報補完で解消できます。

進め方: ①`exceptions` 設定の有効化とエラー修正 → ②独自ルール5本の実装(ソース+テスト+フィクスチャ+ドキュメント+登録) → ③新ルールが自分自身のコードに出す違反の修正 → ④全ゲート(phpstan / phpunit / loc-guard / tree-guard / deptrac / cs-fixer)の通過確認、の順でやります。まずタスク登録と既存コードの規約確認から始めます。

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace PhpAiToolkit\PhpStan\Rule;

use PhpAiToolkit\PhpStan\Rule\NoControlFlowInTestMethod\TestMethodControlFlowErrorCollector;
use PhpAiToolkit\PhpStan\Rule\Shared\TestMethodDetector;
use PhpAiToolkit\PhpStan\Support\TestClassScope;
use PHPStan\Analyser\Scope;
use PHPStan\Rules\IdentifierRuleError;
use PHPStan\Rules\Rule;

/**
 * @implements Rule<\PhpParser\Node\Stmt\ClassMethod>
 */
final class NoControlFlowInTestMethodRule implements Rule
{
    /** @readonly */
    private TestMethodDetector $testMethodDetector;

    /** @readonly */
    private TestMethodControlFlowErrorCollector $errorCollector;

    /**
     * @param TestClassScope $testClassScope test class scope detector
     */
    public function __construct(
        /** @readonly */
        private TestClassScope $testClassScope,
        ?TestMethodDetector $testMethodDetector = null,
        ?TestMethodControlFlowErrorCollector $errorCollector = null,
    ) {
        $this->testMethodDetector = $testMethodDetector ?? new TestMethodDetector();
        $this->errorCollector = $errorCollector ?? new TestMethodControlFlowErrorCollector();
    }

    /**
     * @return class-string<\PhpParser\Node\Stmt\ClassMethod>
     */
    public function getNodeType(): string
    {
        return \PhpParser\Node\Stmt\ClassMethod::class;
    }

    /**
     * @param \PhpParser\Node\Stmt\ClassMethod $node
     * @return list<IdentifierRuleError>
     */
    public function processNode(\PhpParser\Node $node, Scope $scope): array
    {
        if (!$this->testClassScope->isRestrictedTestClass($scope)) {
            return [];
        }

        if (!$this->testMethodDetector->isTestMethod($node)) {
            return [];
        }

        if ($node->stmts === null) {
            return [];
        }

        $methodName = $node->name->toString();

        return $this->errorCollector->errors($node->stmts, $methodName);
    }
}

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace PhpAiToolkit\PhpStan\Rule;

use PhpAiToolkit\PhpStan\Rule\Shared\FileTokenParser;
use PhpAiToolkit\PhpStan\Rule\Shared\ForbiddenCommentTokenAnalyzer;
use PHPStan\Analyser\Scope;
use PHPStan\Node\FileNode;
use PHPStan\Rules\IdentifierRuleError;
use PHPStan\Rules\Rule;

/**
 * @implements Rule<FileNode>
 */
final class ForbiddenCommentRule implements Rule
{
    /** @readonly */
    private FileTokenParser $fileTokenParser;

    /** @readonly */
    private ForbiddenCommentTokenAnalyzer $tokenAnalyzer;

    /**
     * Creates the rule from tokenizer parsing and token analysis.
     */
    public function __construct(?FileTokenParser $fileTokenParser = null, ?ForbiddenCommentTokenAnalyzer $tokenAnalyzer = null)
    {
        $this->fileTokenParser = $fileTokenParser ?? new FileTokenParser();
        $this->tokenAnalyzer = $tokenAnalyzer ?? new ForbiddenCommentTokenAnalyzer();
    }

    /**
     * @return class-string<FileNode>
     */
    public function getNodeType(): string
    {
        return FileNode::class;
    }

    /**
     * @param FileNode $node
     * @return list<IdentifierRuleError>
     */
    public function processNode(\PhpParser\Node $node, Scope $scope): array
    {
        unset($node);

        $tokens = $this->fileTokenParser->parse($scope->getFile());
        if ($tokens === null) {
            return [];
        }

        return $this->tokenAnalyzer->errors($tokens);
    }
}

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  COMPOSER_NO_INTERACTION: '1'

jobs:
  tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - php: '8.0'
            test-script: test:unit:legacy
          - php: '8.1'
            test-script: test:unit
          - php: '8.2'
            test-script: test:unit
          - php: '8.3'
            test-script: test:unit
          - php: '8.4'
            test-script: test:unit
          - php: '8.5'
            test-script: test:unit
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@9c091bb21b7c1c1d1991bb908d89e4e9dddfe3e0 # v7.0.0

      - uses: shivammathur/setup-php@f3e473d116dcccaddc5834248c87452386958240 # 2.37.2
        with:
          php-version: ${{ matrix.php }}
          extensions: mbstring, pcntl
          coverage: none

      - run: cp "composer.lock.php-${{ matrix.php }}" composer.lock

      - uses: ramsey/composer-install@65e4f84970763564f46a70b8a54b90d033b3bdda # 4.0.0
        with:
          dependency-versions: locked
          composer-options: --prefer-dist

      - run: composer ${{ matrix.test-script }}

  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        php:
          - '8.0'
          - '8.1'
          - '8.2'
          - '8.3'
          - '8.4'
          - '8.5'

      - uses: actions/checkout@9c091bb21b7c1c1d1991bb908d89e4e9dddfe3e0 # v7.0.0

      - run: cp "composer.lock.php-${{ matrix.php }}" composer.lock

      - run: composer validate --strict --no-check-publish

      - uses: ramsey/composer-install@65e4f84970763564f46a70b8a54b90d033b3bdda # 4.0.0
        with:
          dependency-versions: locked
          composer-options: --prefer-dist

      - run: composer format:check

      - run: composer phpstan

      - run: composer compat

      - run: composer loc-guard

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace PhpAiToolkit\PhpStan\Rule\NoControlFlowInTestMethod;

use PhpParser\NodeFinder;
use PHPStan\Rules\IdentifierRuleError;
use PHPStan\Rules\RuleErrorBuilder;

/**
 * Collects control-flow violations from one test method body.
 */
final class TestMethodControlFlowErrorCollector
{
    /** @readonly */
    private ControlFlowTypeResolver $typeResolver;

    /** @readonly */
    private NestedScopeFilter $nestedScopeFilter;

    /**
     * Creates a collector from type resolution and nested-scope filtering.
     */
    public function __construct(
        ?ControlFlowTypeResolver $typeResolver = null,
        ?NestedScopeFilter $nestedScopeFilter = null,
    ) {
        $this->typeResolver = $typeResolver ?? new ControlFlowTypeResolver();
        $this->nestedScopeFilter = $nestedScopeFilter ?? new NestedScopeFilter();
    }

    /**
     * @param array<\PhpParser\Node\Stmt> $stmts
     * @return list<IdentifierRuleError>
     */
    public function errors(array $stmts, string $methodName): array
    {
        $nodeFinder = new NodeFinder();
        $violations = $nodeFinder->find($stmts, function (\PhpParser\Node $node): bool {
            return $this->typeResolver->type($node) !== null;
        });

        $filtered = $this->nestedScopeFilter->filter($violations, $stmts);

        $errors = [];
        foreach ($filtered as $node) {
            $statementType = $this->typeResolver->type($node);
            if ($statementType === null) {
                continue;
            }

            $errors[] = RuleErrorBuilder::message(
                sprintf(
                    'Split test method %s() so it contains no "%s" statement. Use separate tests or a data provider for each case.',
                    $methodName,
                    $statementType
                )
            )
                ->identifier('customRules.testMethodControlFlow')
                ->line($node->getStartLine())
                ->build();
        }

        return $errors;
    }
}

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace PhpAiToolkit\PhpStan\Rule\Shared;

use ParseError;

/**
 * Parses PHP files into native tokenizer tokens for file-level rules.
 */
final class FileTokenParser
{
    /**
     * Returns tokenizer tokens for a readable PHP file, or null when unavailable.
     *
     * @return array<int, array{int, string, int}|string>|null
     */
    public function parse(string $path): ?array
    {
        if (!is_file($path) || !is_readable($path)) {
            return null;
        }

        $source = file_get_contents($path);
        if ($source === false) {
            return null;
        }

        try {
            return token_get_all($source, TOKEN_PARSE);
        } catch (ParseError) {
            return null;
        }
    }
}

# PHPStan Rules

Custom PHPStan rules provided by php-ai-toolkit. Each rule detects anti-patterns that actually occur in AI-generated code.

## General

Rules applied to all code.

| Rule | Description | Error Identifier |
|------|-------------|------------------|
| [ForbiddenCommentRule](rules/ForbiddenCommentRule.md) | Forbids `@phpstan-ignore` and `@infection-ignore-all` comments | `customRules.phpstanIgnoreComment`, `customRules.infectionIgnoreAllComment` |
| [ForbiddenMagicMethodCallRule](rules/ForbiddenMagicMethodCallRule.md) | Forbids direct calls to magic methods | `customRules.forbiddenMagicMethodCall` |
| [ForbiddenNamespaceRule](rules/ForbiddenNamespaceRule.md) | Forbids configured namespace prefixes such as `Tests\Support`, `Tests\Helper`, and `Tests\Util` | `customRules.forbiddenNamespace` |
| [OverrideMustHaveAttributeRule](rules/OverrideMustHaveAttributeRule.md) | Requires `#[Override]` attribute on overridden methods | `customRules.overrideMustHaveAttribute` |
| [SrcUnitTestPairRule](rules/SrcUnitTestPairRule.md) | Enforces 1:1 pairing between `src/` classes and `tests/Unit/` test classes | `customRules.srcUnitTestPair` |
| [RequirePhpDocOnPublicApiRule](rules/RequirePhpDocOnPublicApiRule.md) | Requires PHPDoc on all public API elements | `customRules.requirePhpDocOnPublicApi` |
| [ForbidNonDocCommentRule](rules/ForbidNonDocCommentRule.md) | Forbids `/* */` and `#` comments everywhere, and `//` comments outside `catch` blocks and array literals; `/** */` PHPDoc is allowed | `customRules.forbidNonDocComment` |
| [ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRule](rules/ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRule.md) | Forbids single-line PHPDoc on public elements; requires multi-line format | `customRules.forbidSingleLinePhpDoc` |
| [ForbidClassLikeNameSuffixRule](rules/ForbidClassLikeNameSuffixRule.md) | Forbids configured suffixes on class, interface, trait, and enum names | `customRules.forbiddenClassLikeNameSuffix` |
| [NoNonPublicMethodRule](rules/NoNonPublicMethodRule.md) | Forbids private methods and forbids protected methods outside abstract classes, traits, and override methods | `customRules.nonPublicMethod` |

## Test Class

Rules applied to test classes in the `Tests\Unit` / `Tests\Integration` namespaces. Rules marked with `*` apply to all `Tests\` namespaces.

| Rule | Description | Error Identifier |
|------|-------------|------------------|
| [NoPropertyInTestClassRule](rules/NoPropertyInTestClassRule.md) | Forbids property declarations in test classes | `customRules.noPropertyInTestClass` |
| [NoClassConstantInTestClassRule](rules/NoClassConstantInTestClassRule.md) | Forbids class constants in test classes | `customRules.noClassConstantInTestClass` |
| [NoPrivateMethodInTestClassRule](rules/NoPrivateMethodInTestClassRule.md) | Forbids private methods in test classes | `customRules.noPrivateMethodInTestClass` |
| [NoHelperMethodInTestClassRule](rules/NoHelperMethodInTestClassRule.md) | Forbids methods other than test/provider/override | `customRules.noHelperMethodInTestClass` |
| [NoControlFlowInTestMethodRule](rules/NoControlFlowInTestMethodRule.md) | Forbids control flow statements in test methods | `customRules.noControlFlowInTestMethod` |
| [NoTraitUseInTestClassRule](rules/NoTraitUseInTestClassRule.md) | Forbids trait usage in test classes | `customRules.noTraitUseInTestClass` |
| [NoReflectionInTestClassRule](rules/NoReflectionInTestClassRule.md) `*` | Forbids Reflection API usage in test classes | `customRules.noReflectionInTestClass` |
| [NoRedundantAssertInstanceOfRule](rules/NoRedundantAssertInstanceOfRule.md) `*` | Forbids redundant PHPUnit `assertInstanceOf()` calls for values with one statically-known type | `customRules.noRedundantAssertInstanceOf` |
| [PhpUnitMockApiRule](rules/PhpUnitMockApiRule.md) `*` | Restricts mock API and enforces interface-only mocking | `customRules.phpUnitMockApi` |
| [ForbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClassRule](rules/ForbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClassRule.md) | Forbids descriptive PHPDoc text in test classes | `customRules.forbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClass` |
| [TestNamingConventionRule](rules/TestNamingConventionRule.md) | Enforces naming conventions for test methods and data providers | `customRules.testNamingConvention` |

## Disabling Rules

To disable a specific rule, suppress its error identifier in your project's `phpstan.neon`:

```neon
parameters:
    ignoreErrors:
        - identifier: customRules.infectionIgnoreAllComment
```

## Parameters

The following parameters can be customized in your project's `phpstan.neon`:

| Parameter | Default | Description |
|-----------|---------|-------------|
| `testNamespacePrefixes` | `['Tests']` | Test namespace prefixes |
| `restrictedTestNamespacePrefixes` | `['Tests\Unit', 'Tests\Integration']` | Test namespaces where strict rules apply |
| `srcUnitTestPairExcludePatterns` | `[]` | Patterns to exclude from test pair checks |
| `srcMarker` | `'/src/'` | Source code path marker |
| `unitTestMarker` | `'/tests/Unit/'` | Unit test path marker |
| `forbiddenNamespacePrefixes` | `['Tests\Support', 'Tests\Supports', 'Tests\Helper', 'Tests\Helpers', 'Tests\Util', 'Tests\Utils', 'Tests\Utility', 'Tests\Utilities']` | Namespace prefixes to forbid |
| `forbiddenClassLikeNameSuffixes` | See [`extension.neon`](../extension.neon) | Class-like declaration name suffixes to forbid |

Fix the 94 baseline errors without ignoreErrors: add @throws tags to direct throwers (LocGuard/TreeGuard), add token_get_all DynamicFunctionThrowTypeExtension for ParseError, resolve dead Throwable catch in AssertInstanceOfTypeMatcher.

content.subject: Implement ForbidEmptyCatchRule
content.description: New PHPStan rule forbidding catch blocks with empty bodies. Source in src/PhpStan/Rule/, test + fixture, docs/rules/ page, extension.neon registration.

content.subject: Implement RequireThrowsTagOnDirectThrowRule
content.description: New PHPStan rule: any exception thrown directly in a function/method body and not caught within it must be declared in @throws (checked or unchecked alike). Handles throw new X and rethrow of caught variable; skips dynamic throws.

content.subject: Implement RequireExceptionChainingRule
content.description: New PHPStan rule: throwing a new exception inside a catch block must pass the caught exception (e.g. as previous). Rethrow of the caught variable itself is allowed; non-binding catch that throws a new exception is a violation.

content.subject: Implement ForbidBroadCatchRule
content.description: New PHPStan rule forbidding catch of Throwable/Exception and LogicException/Error subtrees outside configured boundary paths (configurable via customRules parameters).

content.subject: Implement ForbidGenericThrowsTagRule
content.description: New PHPStan rule forbidding @throws \Exception and @throws \Throwable declarations; concrete exception types required.

content.subject: Update docs, AGENTS.md, and pass all quality gates
content.description: Update docs/phpstan-rules.md, docs/phpstan.md (exceptions section), AGENTS.md (rule count 21→26, doc list), README if it lists rules. Run composer lint (phpstan, compat, loc-guard, tree-guard, deptrac, format:check) and composer test until green.

1	# PHPStan Configuration Guide
2	
3	PHPStan configuration generated by the `/setup-toolkit-phpstan` skill.
4	
5	## Configuration
6	
7	```neon
8	includes:
9	    - vendor/phpstan/phpstan-strict-rules/rules.neon
10	    - vendor/k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit/extension.neon
11	    - vendor/k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit/error-formatter.neon
12	
13	parameters:
14	    level: max
15	    paths:
16	        - src
17	        - tests
18	```
19	
20	## Explanation
21	
22	### `level: max`
23	
24	Sets PHPStan analysis level to the maximum.
25	
26	**Why:** Raising the PHPStan level mid-project produces a flood of errors, making gradual migration difficult. Starting at max catches type inconsistencies from the very beginning. When an AI agent generates type-mismatched code, it gets immediate feedback and is forced to fix it.
27	
28	### `phpstan-strict-rules`
29	
30	Adds the official PHPStan strict rule set.
31	
32	**Why:** PHP permits patterns that are technically valid but practically bug-prone: type juggling with `==`, unused parameters, unsafe casts, etc. Strict rules detect these statically. When an AI agent generates these patterns, they are reported as errors.
33	
34	### `extension.neon` (php-ai-toolkit rules)
35	
36	Enables custom rules that detect anti-patterns from AI code generation.
37	
38	**Why:** Standard PHPStan rules do not cover project-specific constraints such as test class structure and comment conventions. See [phpstan-rules.md](phpstan-rules.md) for details.
39	
40	### `error-formatter.neon` (AI error formatter)
41	
42	Formats PHPStan error output for AI agent consumption.
43	
44	**Why:** PHPStan's default error output is designed for humans. AI agents sometimes fail to interpret the context—file paths, line numbers, fix hints—correctly. The AI formatter structures this output to improve the accuracy of AI-driven fixes.
45	
46	### `paths: [src, tests]`
47

# PHPStan Configuration Guide

PHPStan configuration generated by the `/setup-toolkit-phpstan` skill.

## Configuration

```neon
includes:
    - vendor/phpstan/phpstan-strict-rules/rules.neon
    - vendor/k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit/extension.neon
    - vendor/k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit/error-formatter.neon

parameters:
    level: max
    paths:
        - src
        - tests
```

## Explanation

### `level: max`

Sets PHPStan analysis level to the maximum.

**Why:** Raising the PHPStan level mid-project produces a flood of errors, making gradual migration difficult. Starting at max catches type inconsistencies from the very beginning. When an AI agent generates type-mismatched code, it gets immediate feedback and is forced to fix it.

### `phpstan-strict-rules`

Adds the official PHPStan strict rule set.

**Why:** PHP permits patterns that are technically valid but practically bug-prone: type juggling with `==`, unused parameters, unsafe casts, etc. Strict rules detect these statically. When an AI agent generates these patterns, they are reported as errors.

### `extension.neon` (php-ai-toolkit rules)

Enables custom rules that detect anti-patterns from AI code generation.

**Why:** Standard PHPStan rules do not cover project-specific constraints such as test class structure and comment conventions. See [phpstan-rules.md](phpstan-rules.md) for details.

### `error-formatter.neon` (AI error formatter)

Formats PHPStan error output for AI agent consumption.

**Why:** PHPStan's default error output is designed for humans. AI agents sometimes fail to interpret the context—file paths, line numbers, fix hints—correctly. The AI formatter structures this output to improve the accuracy of AI-driven fixes.

### `paths: [src, tests]`

Includes both `src` and `tests` in the analysis scope.

**Why:** Since AI agents also generate test code, the same static analysis must apply to tests. Type errors in test code undermine test reliability.

# php-ai-toolkit

A PHPStan extension that detects anti-patterns commonly introduced by AI code generation, plus output formatters optimized for both AI agents and humans.

## Requirements

- PHP ^8.0
- PHPStan ^1.12 || ^2.0
- PHPUnit ^9.6 || ^10.5 || ^11 || ^12 || ^13

The PHPUnit test reporter supports PHPUnit 9.6 and 10.5 or later through
version-specific adapters. PHPUnit 10+ uses the event extension API, while
PHPUnit 9.6 uses the legacy listener API.

## Quick Start

### 1. Install

This package is not published on Packagist. Install it from the VCS repository by adding the repository to your `composer.json`:

```json
{
    "repositories": [
        {
            "type": "vcs",
            "url": "https://github.com/k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit.git"
        }
    ]
}
```

Then require it as a dev dependency:

```bash
composer require --dev k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit
```

### 2. Install AI Agent Skills

```bash
vendor/bin/php-ai-toolkit install
```

Auto-detects AI agent directories (`.claude`, `.agents`, `.continue`, etc.) in your project root and installs skills. Use `--force` to overwrite, `--copy` to copy instead of symlinking.

### 3. Run setup skills

Run the following skills in your AI agent:

- `/setup-toolkit-phpstan` — PHPStan at level max with strict rules and AI error formatter
- `/setup-toolkit-phpunit` — PHPUnit with strict configuration and AI test reporter
- `/setup-toolkit-php-cs-fixer` — PHP-CS-Fixer configuration

- `/setup-toolkit-tree-guard` — TreeGuard directory and file structure constraints

- `/setup-toolkit-github-actions` — GitHub Actions CI for tests, lint gates, PHP compatibility, and pinned actions
- `/setup-toolkit-agents-md` — AGENTS.md with project conventions and AI agent guidelines

Each skill reads your project structure and generates appropriate configuration.

## Documentation

MIT

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace PhpAiToolkit\LocGuard\Cli;

use function array_shift;

use Closure;
use PhpAiToolkit\LocGuard\Analysis\LocGuardAnalyzer;
use PhpAiToolkit\LocGuard\Config\ConfigLoader;
use PhpAiToolkit\LocGuard\LocGuardException;
use PhpAiToolkit\LocGuard\Reporting\ReporterFactory;

use function sprintf;

/**
 * CLI entry point for LocGuard.
 */
final class Application
{
    private const VERSION = '1.0.0';

    /** @readonly */
    private LocGuardOutputWriter $writer;

    /** @readonly */
    private LocGuardCliArgumentParser $argumentParser;

    /** @readonly */
    private LocGuardHelpText $helpText;

    /** @readonly */
    private LocGuardAnalysisRunner $analysisRunner;

    /** @readonly */
    private ConfigLoader $configLoader;

    /** @readonly */
    private LocGuardAnalyzer $analyzer;

    /** @readonly */
    private ReporterFactory $reporterFactory;

    /**
     * Creates the LocGuard CLI application for a project working directory.
     */
    public function __construct(
        /** @readonly */
        private string $workingDirectory,
        ?ConfigLoader $configLoader = null,
        ?LocGuardAnalyzer $analyzer = null,
        ?ReporterFactory $reporterFactory = null,
        ?Closure $stdout = null,
        ?Closure $stderr = null,
        ?LocGuardCliArgumentParser $argumentParser = null,
        ?LocGuardHelpText $helpText = null,
        ?LocGuardAnalysisRunner $analysisRunner = null,
    ) {
        $this->configLoader = $configLoader ?? new ConfigLoader();
        $this->analyzer = $analyzer ?? new LocGuardAnalyzer();
        $this->reporterFactory = $reporterFactory ?? new ReporterFactory();
        $this->writer = new LocGuardOutputWriter($stdout, $stderr);
        $this->argumentParser = $argumentParser ?? new LocGuardCliArgumentParser();
        $this->helpText = $helpText ?? new LocGuardHelpText();
        $this->analysisRunner = $analysisRunner ?? new LocGuardAnalysisRunner(
            $this->workingDirectory,
            $this->configLoader,
            $this->analyzer,
            $this->reporterFactory,
            $this->writer,
        );
    }

    /**
     * @param list<string> $argv
     */
    public function run(array $argv): int
    {
        array_shift($argv);
        try {
            $arguments = $this->argumentParser->parse($argv);
        } catch (LocGuardException $exception) {
            $this->writer->writeError(sprintf("LocGuard error: %s\n", $exception->getMessage()));

            return 2;
        }

        if ($arguments['help']) {
            $this->writer->write($this->helpText->text());

            return 0;
        }

        if ($arguments['version']) {
            $this->writer->write(sprintf("loc-guard %s\n", self::VERSION));

            return 0;
        }

        return $this->analysisRunner->run($arguments['config'], $arguments['reporter']);
    }
}

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace PhpAiToolkit\LocGuard\Cli;

use PhpAiToolkit\LocGuard\Analysis\LocGuardAnalyzer;
use PhpAiToolkit\LocGuard\Config\ConfigLoader;
use PhpAiToolkit\LocGuard\LocGuardException;
use PhpAiToolkit\LocGuard\Reporting\ReporterFactory;

use function sprintf;

/**
 * Runs LocGuard analysis from resolved CLI options.
 */
final class LocGuardAnalysisRunner
{
    /** @readonly */
    private LocGuardConfigPathResolver $pathResolver;

    /** @readonly */
    private LocGuardReporterOverride $reporterOverride;

    /**
     * Creates an analysis runner from LocGuard services.
     */
    public function __construct(
        /** @readonly */
        private string $workingDirectory,
        /** @readonly */
        private ConfigLoader $configLoader,
        /** @readonly */
        private LocGuardAnalyzer $analyzer,
        /** @readonly */
        private ReporterFactory $reporterFactory,
        /** @readonly */
        private LocGuardOutputWriter $writer,
        ?LocGuardConfigPathResolver $pathResolver = null,
        ?LocGuardReporterOverride $reporterOverride = null,
    ) {
        $this->pathResolver = $pathResolver ?? new LocGuardConfigPathResolver();
        $this->reporterOverride = $reporterOverride ?? new LocGuardReporterOverride();
    }

    /**
     * Runs analysis and writes the selected report.
     */
    public function run(string $configPath, ?string $reporterOverride): int
    {
        try {
            $config = $this->configLoader->load($this->pathResolver->resolve($this->workingDirectory, $configPath));
            $config = $this->reporterOverride->apply($config, $reporterOverride);
            $result = $this->analyzer->analyze($config);
            $reporter = $this->reporterFactory->create($config->report->reporter);
        } catch (LocGuardException $exception) {
            $this->writer->writeError(sprintf("LocGuard error: %s\n", $exception->getMessage()));

            return 2;
        }

        $this->writer->write($reporter->report($result, $config->report));

        return $result->hasViolations() ? 1 : 0;
    }
}

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace PhpAiToolkit\PhpStan\Rule\NoRedundantAssertInstanceOf;

use function is_a;

use PHPStan\Type\ObjectType;
use PHPStan\Type\Type;
use Throwable;

/**
 * Compares assertInstanceOf() expected and actual static types.
 */
final class AssertInstanceOfTypeMatcher
{
    /**
     * Reports whether the actual static type is already guaranteed to satisfy the expected type.
     */
    public function matches(string $expectedTypeName, Type $actualType, string $actualTypeName): bool
    {
        if ($actualTypeName === $expectedTypeName) {
            return true;
        }

        try {
            return (new ObjectType($expectedTypeName))->isSuperTypeOf($actualType)->yes();
        } catch (Throwable $exception) {
            if (!is_a($exception, 'PHPStan\Reflection\MissingStaticAccessorInstanceException')) {
                throw $exception;
            }

            return false;
        }
    }
}

    }

1	# TreeGuard Configuration
2	
3	TreeGuard configuration generated by the `/setup-toolkit-tree-guard` skill.
4	
5	## Purpose
6	
7	TreeGuard is a first-party CLI for enforcing directory and file structure constraints. It checks directory file counts, subdirectory counts, recursive subtree totals, nesting depth, file and directory naming (globs and case conventions), required files, and empty directories. It catches the structural drift AI agents tend to introduce — bloated directories, naming deviations, missing required files, deep nesting, and leftover empty directories — before it accumulates.
8	
9	## Command
10	
11	Run:
12	
13	```bash
14	vendor/bin/tree-guard --config=tree.yaml
15	```
16	
17	Exit codes:
18	
19	- `0`: no violations
20	- `1`: structure violations found
21	- `2`: configuration or runtime error
22	
23	## Configuration
24	
25	Example `tree.yaml`:
26	
27	```yaml
28	paths:
29	  - src
30	
31	exclude: []
32	
33	rules:
34	  - path: 'src/**'
35	    forbid_empty: true
36	    allow: ['*.php']
37	    deny: ['*Helper.php']
38	    file_case: pascal
39	    dir_case: pascal
40	    max_files: 25
41	    max_dirs: 20
42	  - path: 'src/*'
43	    max_total_files: 250
44	    max_depth: 3
45	
46	report:
47	  reporter: ai
48	  order_by:
49	    - path
50	    - rule
51	```
52	
53	`paths` (default `['src']`) lists the directories to scan, relative to the config file directory. Each entry must exist and be a directory.
54	
55	`exclude` (default `[]`) removes entries from analysis. An excluded file disappears from its directory listing; an excluded directory is pruned together with its whole subtree.
56	
57	`rules` (default `[]`) is a list of rule blocks. Each block has a required `path` pattern and any number of constraints. Every rule whose pattern matches a directory is applied to it independently; there is no override or merge between overlapping rules. Violations carry the originating pattern, so each rule's findings stay identifiable.
58	
59	Unknown keys in a rule block are rejected with an error. A typo such as `max_file` would otherwise silently disable a constraint.
60	
61	## Pattern Semantics
62	
63	`rules[].path` patterns match whole relative directory paths segment by segment:
64	
65	- The pattern and the path are split on `/`. Every non-`**` segment is matched against exactly one path segment with `fnmatch`, so `*` never crosses a `/` boundary.
66	- A `**` segment matches **zero or more** path segments. This means `src/**` also matches `src` itself — unlike gitignore, where `src/**` matches only paths inside `src`.
67	- Patterns are anchored at both ends: `PhpStan/Rule` does not match `src/PhpStan/Rule`.
68	
69	Examples: `src` matches only `src`; `src/*` matches only direct children of `src`; `src/**` matches `src` and everything below it; `**/Rule` matches a directory named `Rule` at any depth.
70	
71	`exclude` uses a different mechanism: each entry is a plain `fnmatch` glob applied to the whole relative path (LocGuard-compatible), where `*` can cross `/` boundaries.
72	
73	## Constraints
74	
75	| Key | Type | Checks |
76	|-----|------|--------|
77	| `max_files` | int ≥ 1 | Number of files directly in the directory. |
78	| `max_dirs` | int ≥ 1 | Number of subdirectories directly in the directory. |
79	| `max_total_files` | int ≥ 1 | Recursive total file count of the subtree. |
80	| `max_depth` | int ≥ 1 | Nesting depth below the matched directory (itself depth 0). Each descendant directory beyond the limit is reported. |

# TreeGuard Configuration

TreeGuard configuration generated by the `/setup-toolkit-tree-guard` skill.

## Purpose

TreeGuard is a first-party CLI for enforcing directory and file structure constraints. It checks directory file counts, subdirectory counts, recursive subtree totals, nesting depth, file and directory naming (globs and case conventions), required files, and empty directories. It catches the structural drift AI agents tend to introduce — bloated directories, naming deviations, missing required files, deep nesting, and leftover empty directories — before it accumulates.

## Command

Run:

```bash
vendor/bin/tree-guard --config=tree.yaml
```

Exit codes:

- `0`: no violations
- `1`: structure violations found
- `2`: configuration or runtime error

## Configuration

Example `tree.yaml`:

```yaml
paths:
  - src

exclude: []

rules:
  - path: 'src/**'
    forbid_empty: true
    allow: ['*.php']
    deny: ['*Helper.php']
    file_case: pascal
    dir_case: pascal
    max_files: 25
    max_dirs: 20
  - path: 'src/*'
    max_total_files: 250
    max_depth: 3

report:
  reporter: ai
  order_by:
    - path
    - rule
```

`paths` (default `['src']`) lists the directories to scan, relative to the config file directory. Each entry must exist and be a directory.

`exclude` (default `[]`) removes entries from analysis. An excluded file disappears from its directory listing; an excluded directory is pruned together with its whole subtree.

`rules` (default `[]`) is a list of rule blocks. Each block has a required `path` pattern and any number of constraints. Every rule whose pattern matches a directory is applied to it independently; there is no override or merge between overlapping rules. Violations carry the originating pattern, so each rule's findings stay identifiable.

Unknown keys in a rule block are rejected with an error. A typo such as `max_file` would otherwise silently disable a constraint.

## Pattern Semantics

`rules[].path` patterns match whole relative directory paths segment by segment:

- The pattern and the path are split on `/`. Every non-`**` segment is matched against exactly one path segment with `fnmatch`, so `*` never crosses a `/` boundary.
- A `**` segment matches **zero or more** path segments. This means `src/**` also matches `src` itself — unlike gitignore, where `src/**` matches only paths inside `src`.
- Patterns are anchored at both ends: `PhpStan/Rule` does not match `src/PhpStan/Rule`.

Examples: `src` matches only `src`; `src/*` matches only direct children of `src`; `src/**` matches `src` and everything below it; `**/Rule` matches a directory named `Rule` at any depth.

`exclude` uses a different mechanism: each entry is a plain `fnmatch` glob applied to the whole relative path (LocGuard-compatible), where `*` can cross `/` boundaries.

## Constraints

| Key | Type | Checks |
|-----|------|--------|
| `max_files` | int ≥ 1 | Number of files directly in the directory. |
| `max_dirs` | int ≥ 1 | Number of subdirectories directly in the directory. |
| `max_total_files` | int ≥ 1 | Recursive total file count of the subtree. |
| `max_depth` | int ≥ 1 | Nesting depth below the matched directory (itself depth 0). Each descendant directory beyond the limit is reported. |

namespace PhpAiToolkit\PhpStan\Rule;

use PhpAiToolkit\PhpStan\Rule\ForbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClass\DescriptivePhpDocErrorCollector;
use PhpAiToolkit\PhpStan\Rule\Shared\RestrictedTestNamespaceMatcher;
use PHPStan\Analyser\Scope;
use PHPStan\Rules\IdentifierRuleError;
use PHPStan\Rules\Rule;

/**
 * Forbids descriptive (non-annotation) PHPDoc text in test classes.
 *
 * In restricted test namespaces, PHPDoc on classes and methods must contain
 * only @tags (e.g. @dataProvider, @extends). Descriptive prose text is forbidden
 * because test names and class names should be self-documenting.
 *
 * @implements Rule<\PhpParser\Node\Stmt\ClassLike>
 */
final class ForbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClassRule implements Rule
{
    /** @readonly */
    private DescriptivePhpDocErrorCollector $errorCollector;

    /**
     * @param list<string> $restrictedTestNamespacePrefixes namespace prefixes for test classes
     */
    public function __construct(
        array $restrictedTestNamespacePrefixes = ['Tests\\Unit', 'Tests\\Integration'],
    ) {
        $this->errorCollector = new DescriptivePhpDocErrorCollector(new RestrictedTestNamespaceMatcher($restrictedTestNamespacePrefixes));
    }

    /**
     * @return class-string<\PhpParser\Node\Stmt\ClassLike>
     */
    public function getNodeType(): string
    {
        return \PhpParser\Node\Stmt\ClassLike::class;
    }

    /**
     * @param \PhpParser\Node\Stmt\ClassLike $node
     * @return list<IdentifierRuleError>
     */
    public function processNode(\PhpParser\Node $node, Scope $scope): array
    {
        return $this->errorCollector->errors($node);
    }
}

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace PhpAiToolkit\LocGuard\Config;

use function dirname;
use function is_array;
use function is_file;

use PhpAiToolkit\LocGuard\LocGuardException;

use function sprintf;

use Symfony\Component\Yaml\Exception\ParseException;
use Symfony\Component\Yaml\Yaml;

/**
 * Loads and validates loc.yaml.
 */
final class ConfigLoader
{
    /** @readonly */
    private ConfigStringListReader $stringListReader;

    /** @readonly */
    private LimitConfigReader $limitConfigReader;

    /** @readonly */
    private ReportConfigReader $reportConfigReader;

    /**
     * Creates a config loader from YAML section readers.
     */
    public function __construct(
        ?ConfigStringListReader $stringListReader = null,
        ?LimitConfigReader $limitConfigReader = null,
        ?ReportConfigReader $reportConfigReader = null,
    ) {
        $this->stringListReader = $stringListReader ?? new ConfigStringListReader();
        $this->limitConfigReader = $limitConfigReader ?? new LimitConfigReader();
        $this->reportConfigReader = $reportConfigReader ?? new ReportConfigReader();
    }

    /**
     * Loads and validates a LocGuard YAML configuration file.
     */
    public function load(string $path): LocGuardConfig
    {
        if (!is_file($path)) {
            throw new LocGuardException(sprintf('LocGuard config not found: %s', $path));
        }

        try {
            $data = Yaml::parseFile($path);
        } catch (ParseException $exception) {
            throw new LocGuardException('Invalid loc.yaml: ' . $exception->getMessage(), 0, $exception);
        }

        if (!is_array($data)) {
            throw new LocGuardException('Invalid loc.yaml: top-level value must be a mapping.');
        }

        return new LocGuardConfig(
            dirname($path),
            $this->stringListReader->read($data, 'paths', ['src']),
            $this->stringListReader->read($data, 'exclude', []),
            $this->limitConfigReader->read($data['limits'] ?? []),
            $this->reportConfigReader->read($data['report'] ?? []),
        );
    }
}

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace PhpAiToolkit\LocGuard\Config;

use function is_int;
use function is_string;

use PhpAiToolkit\LocGuard\LocGuardException;

use function sprintf;

/**
 * Reads scalar values from loc.yaml mappings.
 */
final class ConfigScalarReader
{
    /**
     * Reads a non-empty string value.
     *
     * @param array<mixed> $data
     */
    public function string(array $data, string $key, string $default): string
    {
        $value = $data[$key] ?? $default;
        if (!is_string($value) || $value === '') {
            throw new LocGuardException(sprintf('Invalid loc.yaml: "%s" must be a non-empty string.', $key));
        }

        return $value;
    }

    /**
     * Reads a positive integer value.
     *
     * @param array<mixed> $data
     */
    public function positiveInt(array $data, string $key, int $default): int
    {
        $value = $data[$key] ?? $default;
        if (!is_int($value) || $value < 1) {
            throw new LocGuardException(sprintf('Invalid loc.yaml: "limits.%s" must be a positive integer.', $key));
        }

        return $value;
    }
}

        }

        if ($reporter === 'text') {

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace PhpAiToolkit\LocGuard\Config;

use function implode;
use function in_array;
use function is_array;

use PhpAiToolkit\LocGuard\LocGuardException;

use function sprintf;

/**
 * Reads LocGuard report configuration from loc.yaml.
 */
final class ReportConfigReader
{
    /** @var list<string> */
    private const REPORTERS = ['ai', 'text', 'json'];

    /** @var list<string> */
    private const ORDER_FIELDS = ['path', 'line', 'rule', 'actual', 'limit'];

    /** @readonly */
    private ConfigScalarReader $scalarReader;

    /** @readonly */
    private ConfigStringListReader $stringListReader;

    /**
     * Creates a reader from scalar and list validation.
     */
    public function __construct(
        ?ConfigScalarReader $scalarReader = null,
        ?ConfigStringListReader $stringListReader = null,
    ) {
        $this->scalarReader = $scalarReader ?? new ConfigScalarReader();
        $this->stringListReader = $stringListReader ?? new ConfigStringListReader();
    }

    /**
     * Reads report output configuration.
     *
     * @param mixed $value
     */
    public function read($value): ReportConfig
    {
        if (!is_array($value)) {
            throw new LocGuardException('Invalid loc.yaml: "report" must be a mapping.');
        }

        $reporter = $this->scalarReader->string($value, 'reporter', 'ai');
        if (!in_array($reporter, self::REPORTERS, true)) {
            throw new LocGuardException(sprintf('Invalid loc.yaml: "report.reporter" must be one of: %s.', implode(', ', self::REPORTERS)));
        }

        $orderBy = $this->stringListReader->read($value, 'order_by', ['path', 'line', 'rule']);
        foreach ($orderBy as $field) {
            if (!in_array($field, self::ORDER_FIELDS, true)) {
                throw new LocGuardException(sprintf('Invalid loc.yaml: "report.order_by" contains unsupported field "%s".', $field));
            }
        }

        return new ReportConfig($reporter, $orderBy);
    }
}

namespace PhpAiToolkit\LocGuard\Filesystem;

use function is_dir;
use function is_file;

use PhpAiToolkit\LocGuard\Config\LocGuardConfig;
use PhpAiToolkit\LocGuard\LocGuardException;
use RecursiveDirectoryIterator;
use RecursiveIteratorIterator;
use SplFileInfo;

use function sprintf;

/**
 * Collects PHP files from one configured absolute path.
 */
final class PhpPathFileCollector
{
    /** @readonly */
    private PhpFileInclusionPolicy $inclusionPolicy;

    /** @readonly */
    private LocGuardPathResolver $pathResolver;

    /**
     * Creates a collector from inclusion and path resolution policies.
     */
    public function __construct(
        ?PhpFileInclusionPolicy $inclusionPolicy = null,
        ?LocGuardPathResolver $pathResolver = null,
    ) {
        $this->inclusionPolicy = $inclusionPolicy ?? new PhpFileInclusionPolicy();
        $this->pathResolver = $pathResolver ?? new LocGuardPathResolver();
    }

    /**
     * Returns PHP files under the configured path.
     *
     * @return array<string, string>
     */
    public function files(LocGuardConfig $config, string $path): array
    {
        if (is_file($path)) {
            return $this->inclusionPolicy->includes($config, $path) ? [$path => $this->pathResolver->relative($config->root, $path)] : [];
        }

        if (!is_dir($path)) {
            throw new LocGuardException(sprintf('Configured path does not exist: %s', $path));
        }

        $files = [];
        $iterator = new RecursiveIteratorIterator(
            new RecursiveDirectoryIterator($path, RecursiveDirectoryIterator::SKIP_DOTS),
        );

        /** @var SplFileInfo $item */
        foreach ($iterator as $item) {
            $file = $item->getPathname();
            if ($this->inclusionPolicy->includes($config, $file)) {
                $files[$file] = $this->pathResolver->relative($config->root, $file);
            }
        }

        return $files;
    }
}

namespace PhpAiToolkit\LocGuard\Config;

use function is_array;
use function is_string;

use PhpAiToolkit\LocGuard\LocGuardException;

use function sprintf;

/**
 * Reads non-empty string lists from loc.yaml mappings.
 */
final class ConfigStringListReader
{
    /**
     * Reads a list of strings from the given key.
     *
     * @param array<mixed> $data
     * @param list<string> $default
     * @return list<string>
     */
    public function read(array $data, string $key, array $default): array
    {
        $value = $data[$key] ?? $default;
        if (!is_array($value)) {
            throw new LocGuardException(sprintf('Invalid loc.yaml: "%s" must be a list of strings.', $key));
        }

        $strings = [];
        foreach ($value as $entry) {
            if (!is_string($entry) || $entry === '') {
                throw new LocGuardException(sprintf('Invalid loc.yaml: "%s" must be a list of strings.', $key));
            }
            $strings[] = $entry;
        }

        return $strings;
    }
}

/**
 * Reads LocGuard numeric limits from loc.yaml.
 */
final class LimitConfigReader
{
    /** @readonly */
    private ConfigScalarReader $scalarReader;

    /**
     * Creates a reader from scalar validation.
     */
    public function __construct(?ConfigScalarReader $scalarReader = null)
    {
        $this->scalarReader = $scalarReader ?? new ConfigScalarReader();
    }

    /**
     * Reads line-count and complexity limits.
     *
     * @param mixed $value
     */
    public function read($value): LimitConfig
    {
        if (!is_array($value)) {
            throw new LocGuardException('Invalid loc.yaml: "limits" must be a mapping.');
        }

        return new LimitConfig(

            $this->scalarReader->positiveInt($value, 'max_interface_lines', 200),

            $this->scalarReader->positiveInt($value, 'max_function_lines', 50),
            $this->scalarReader->positiveInt($value, 'max_method_lines', 50),

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace PhpAiToolkit\LocGuard\Cli;

use function count;

use PhpAiToolkit\LocGuard\LocGuardException;

use function sprintf;

/**
 * Parses LocGuard command-line arguments.
 */
final class LocGuardCliArgumentParser
{
    /**
     * Parses LocGuard flags and options.
     *
     * @param list<string> $argv
     * @return array{config: string, help: bool, reporter: ?string, version: bool}
     */
    public function parse(array $argv): array
    {
        $arguments = ['config' => 'loc.yaml', 'help' => false, 'reporter' => null, 'version' => false];

        for ($index = 0; $index < count($argv); $index++) {
            $arg = $argv[$index];
            if ($arg === '--help' || $arg === '-h') {
                $arguments['help'] = true;
            } elseif ($arg === '--version' || $arg === '-V') {
                $arguments['version'] = true;
            } elseif ($arg === '--config') {
                if (!isset($argv[$index + 1]) || str_starts_with($argv[$index + 1], '-')) {
                    throw new LocGuardException(sprintf('Missing value for %s.', '--config'));
                }
                $arguments['config'] = $argv[++$index];
            } elseif (str_starts_with($arg, '--config=')) {
                $arguments['config'] = substr($arg, 9);
            } elseif ($arg === '--reporter' || $arg === '--format') {
                if (!isset($argv[$index + 1]) || str_starts_with($argv[$index + 1], '-')) {
                    throw new LocGuardException(sprintf('Missing value for %s.', $arg));
                }
                $arguments['reporter'] = $argv[++$index];
            } elseif (str_starts_with($arg, '--reporter=')) {
                $arguments['reporter'] = substr($arg, 11);
            } elseif (str_starts_with($arg, '--format=')) {
                $arguments['reporter'] = substr($arg, 9);
            } else {
                throw new LocGuardException(sprintf('Unknown option: %s', $arg));
            }
        }

        return $arguments;
    }
}

 */
final class ReportConfigReader
{
    /** @var list<string> */
    private const REPORTERS = ['ai', 'text', 'json'];

    /** @var list<string> */
    private const ORDER_FIELDS = ['path', 'line', 'rule', 'actual', 'limit'];

    /** @readonly */
    private ConfigScalarReader $scalarReader;

    /** @readonly */
    private ConfigStringListReader $stringListReader;

    /**
     * Creates a reader from scalar and list validation.
     */
    public function __construct(
        ?ConfigScalarReader $scalarReader = null,
        ?ConfigStringListReader $stringListReader = null,
    ) {
        $this->scalarReader = $scalarReader ?? new ConfigScalarReader();
        $this->stringListReader = $stringListReader ?? new ConfigStringListReader();
    }

    /**
     * Reads report output configuration.
     *
     * @param mixed $value
     */
    public function read($value): ReportConfig
    {
        if (!is_array($value)) {
            throw new LocGuardException('Invalid loc.yaml: "report" must be a mapping.');
        }

        $reporter = $this->scalarReader->string($value, 'reporter', 'ai');
        if (!in_array($reporter, self::REPORTERS, true)) {
            throw new LocGuardException(sprintf('Invalid loc.yaml: "report.reporter" must be one of: %s.', implode(', ', self::REPORTERS)));
        }

        $orderBy = $this->stringListReader->read($value, 'order_by', ['path', 'line', 'rule']);
        foreach ($orderBy as $field) {
            if (!in_array($field, self::ORDER_FIELDS, true)) {
                throw new LocGuardException(sprintf('Invalid loc.yaml: "report.order_by" contains unsupported field "%s".', $field));
            }
        }

        return new ReportConfig($reporter, $orderBy);
    }
}

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace PhpAiToolkit\LocGuard\Filesystem;

use function is_dir;
use function is_file;

use PhpAiToolkit\LocGuard\Config\LocGuardConfig;
use PhpAiToolkit\LocGuard\LocGuardException;
use RecursiveDirectoryIterator;
use RecursiveIteratorIterator;
use SplFileInfo;

use function sprintf;

/**
 * Collects PHP files from one configured absolute path.
 */
final class PhpPathFileCollector
{
    /** @readonly */
    private PhpFileInclusionPolicy $inclusionPolicy;

    /** @readonly */
    private LocGuardPathResolver $pathResolver;

    /**
     * Creates a collector from inclusion and path resolution policies.
     */
    public function __construct(
        ?PhpFileInclusionPolicy $inclusionPolicy = null,
        ?LocGuardPathResolver $pathResolver = null,
    ) {
        $this->inclusionPolicy = $inclusionPolicy ?? new PhpFileInclusionPolicy();
        $this->pathResolver = $pathResolver ?? new LocGuardPathResolver();
    }

    /**
     * Returns PHP files under the configured path.
     *
     * @return array<string, string>
     */
    public function files(LocGuardConfig $config, string $path): array
    {
        if (is_file($path)) {
            return $this->inclusionPolicy->includes($config, $path) ? [$path => $this->pathResolver->relative($config->root, $path)] : [];
        }

        if (!is_dir($path)) {
            throw new LocGuardException(sprintf('Configured path does not exist: %s', $path));
        }

        $files = [];
        $iterator = new RecursiveIteratorIterator(
            new RecursiveDirectoryIterator($path, RecursiveDirectoryIterator::SKIP_DOTS),
        );

        /** @var SplFileInfo $item */
        foreach ($iterator as $item) {
            $file = $item->getPathname();
            if ($this->inclusionPolicy->includes($config, $file)) {
                $files[$file] = $this->pathResolver->relative($config->root, $file);
            }
        }

        return $files;
    }
}

namespace PhpAiToolkit\LocGuard\Cli;

use function count;

use PhpAiToolkit\LocGuard\LocGuardException;

use function sprintf;

/**
 * Parses LocGuard command-line arguments.
 */
final class LocGuardCliArgumentParser
{
    /**
     * Parses LocGuard flags and options.
     *
     * @param list<string> $argv
     * @return array{config: string, help: bool, reporter: ?string, version: bool}
     */
    public function parse(array $argv): array
    {
        $arguments = ['config' => 'loc.yaml', 'help' => false, 'reporter' => null, 'version' => false];

        for ($index = 0; $index < count($argv); $index++) {
            $arg = $argv[$index];
            if ($arg === '--help' || $arg === '-h') {
                $arguments['help'] = true;
            } elseif ($arg === '--version' || $arg === '-V') {
                $arguments['version'] = true;
            } elseif ($arg === '--config') {
                if (!isset($argv[$index + 1]) || str_starts_with($argv[$index + 1], '-')) {
                    throw new LocGuardException(sprintf('Missing value for %s.', '--config'));
                }
                $arguments['config'] = $argv[++$index];
            } elseif (str_starts_with($arg, '--config=')) {
                $arguments['config'] = substr($arg, 9);
            } elseif ($arg === '--reporter' || $arg === '--format') {
                if (!isset($argv[$index + 1]) || str_starts_with($argv[$index + 1], '-')) {
                    throw new LocGuardException(sprintf('Missing value for %s.', $arg));
                }
                $arguments['reporter'] = $argv[++$index];
            } elseif (str_starts_with($arg, '--reporter=')) {
                $arguments['reporter'] = substr($arg, 11);
            } elseif (str_starts_with($arg, '--format=')) {
                $arguments['reporter'] = substr($arg, 9);
            } else {
                throw new LocGuardException(sprintf('Unknown option: %s', $arg));
            }
        }

        return $arguments;
    }
}

final class ConfigStringListReader
{
    /**

    public function read(array $data, string $key, array $default, string $context): array

        foreach ($value as $entry) {
            if (!is_string($entry) || $entry === '') {
                throw new TreeGuardException(sprintf('Invalid tree.yaml: "%s" must be a list of strings.', $this->label($context, $key)));

        }

        return $strings;
    }

     * Reads an optional list of non-empty strings, returning null when the key is absent.
     *
     * @param array<mixed> $data

    }
